title: She Wrote The Forfeit Rule. It Disqualified Her Own Kid.
script: A team mom on our rec soccer league decided her son's team should never have to forfeit for a scheduling conflict, only the other teams should. She cornered me, the volunteer scheduler, at pickup and insisted I add a clause to the league bylaws letting any coach formally challenge a forfeit within 48 hours for irregular scheduling influence, then copied the league president to make sure I complied. Fine. I added her clause exactly as dictated. Her son's team hit a bye-week conflict two rounds later. The opposing coach, who had been copied on her own email the whole time, filed the exact challenge she had demanded I write into the rules. The league upheld it. Nobody even had to raise their voice. Her son's team was disqualified from the tournament on the rule she wrote herself, and she spent the banquet explaining to twelve nine year olds why mom's rule beat them.
